## Overview

This vignette prepares the data to be used to parameterise the Integral Projection model. It was generated by combining the steps of `dipm_prepdata.R` and `prep-DDDdata`, from the `DDDEvo` package.

## Setup

Loading the required packages.

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
```

Loading the raw data files.

### Loading the pedigree data

```{r }
# getting the pedigree datafile
pedigree <- read.csv2(file.path(here::here(), 'data-raw', 'Pedigree.csv'), header=T) %>%
    as.tibble()
str(pedigree)
# this file is structured according to marking and recapture forms from the field. The information is redundant. To solve this, I will only consider the marking form, reporting individuals at their first capture, and containing the informations on parents.
pedigree <- pedigree %>%
    filter(Form == Cohort)

range(pedigree$Form) #checking how far in time this goes
# I need to match the time specification of the MR dataset, which is by 'sampling'. Given that sampling starts from March 2008 and proceeds monthly, and that the form specification is the form YYMM, I can sort the Form here by numerical order, and assign increasing integers as sampling. 
sampling <- sort(unique(pedigree$Form))
# April 2008 is missing from pedigree file (no new borns big enough after only one month from introduction), so I need to add it manually to avoid the messing up of the sampling order
sampling <- c(803,804,sort(unique(pedigree$Form))[-1])
# going from March 2008 to April 2013 the number of sampling here should be 10+12*4+4=62
# --> checking this
length(sampling)==10+12*4+4

# now the position on the sorted vector corresponds to the sampling month. I can use match to create a sampling column
pedigree$sampling <- match(pedigree$Form, sampling)
# I can do the same for cohort, first and last capture
pedigree$cohort_samp <- match(pedigree$Cohort, sampling)
pedigree$last_samp <- match(pedigree$Last_Capture, sampling)
pedigree$first_samp <- match(pedigree$First_capture, sampling)
```

### Loading the mark-recapture data

```{r }
# read MR datafile
gmrdata <- read.csv(file.path(here::here(), 'data-raw', 'GuppyData_LL.csv'), header=TRUE) %>%
     as.tibble()

# Since I am analysing reproduction, I need the pedigree data to extend past the mark-recapture data by two months (so I can capture individuals born two months after the last observed sampling in gmr)

#### Very early on, I am subsetting the entire dataset for FEMALES ONLY
# This is because, if I calculate local and landscape density here, for which
# I run GLMM later, I will generate male-and-female-density specific resposnes,
# which I won't be able to carry through in the IPM, since only females are accounted!!!
data <- gmrdata %>% filter(stream == 'LL',
                           sampling <= max(pedigree$sampling) - 2,
                           sex == "F")
str(data)

# One fish was captured several times in a month:
nrow(data)
nrow(unique(data[, c("FishID", "sampling")]))
x <- table(interaction(data$FishID, data$sampling))
x[which(x > 1)]
# It is probably important to fix/remove this duplicate, because it results in
# cascading duplications after the successive left_join() calls further down
# this script.
# it looks likely there was a typo during the form filling for one of these fish:
as.data.frame(data %>% filter(FishID == "FLL-4V6K-1302" & sampling == 60))
# We decide to remove the row for the capture from a riffle:
data <- data %>%
    filter(!(FishID == "FLL-4V6K-1302" & sampling == 60 & location == "R56-58L"))
# Even if the data for this particular fish is uncertain, this will be of
# little consequence in the analysis since the entry occurs towards the end of
# the study period for this project (2013-02)

# At this stage the number of rows in the dataset is:
NROW_CHECK <- nrow(data) # 26324 females
# and this should not change during the rest of the script since we do only
# left_join() operations to grow the dataset.


# NOW the MR datafile and the pedigree file should be on the same level
# Below I will calculate the variables I'm interested in: survival, reproduction and dispersal, but first...


# MATERNITY AND PATERNITY
# Adding a column for each individuals father and mother
pedigree.Table <- pedigree %>% select(FishID, Paternity, Maternity) %>%
    unique()
# Convert Paternity and Maternity to strings
pedigree.Table$Paternity = as.character(pedigree.Table$Paternity)
pedigree.Table$Maternity = as.character(pedigree.Table$Maternity)
data <- data %>% left_join(pedigree.Table, by = "FishID")
```

## Processing Data

### Survival

This step will come in handy later. I can add a column of individual survival to time `t+1`. I can make a very rough approximation, and given the very high recapture rate, say that if I never again capture an invidual, it means it's dead.

```{r}
# First we can collect the last month of capture for each fish,
# and as a bonus the info on the first capture too:
id2lastCapture <- data %>% select(FishID, sampling) %>%
    group_by(FishID) %>%
    summarize(lastCapture = max(sampling),
              firstCapture = min(sampling))
# Next we merge it with the full data and add the "surv" column
data <- data %>% left_join(id2lastCapture, by = "FishID") %>%
    mutate(surv = as.numeric(sampling < lastCapture))
# Checking whether the surv information and the survival (pre-existing in the dataset) info correspond.
table(data$surv==data$survival)
# Not always. Let's see when it doesn't:
table(data$surv==data$survival, data$sampling)
# Most issues seem to appear late, which makes sense since according to the way I am calculating surv all individuals must be dead by the end of the dataset (since no sampling > max sampling, even though the observation continues.)
# I will just use survival instead of surv. Removing the confusing column

data <- data %>%
  select(- surv)
```

### Reproduction

```{r }
# deriving how many offspring are produced by each individual in a month

# NOTE! I do not think I need to correct for non-captured individuals which 
# produce offspring here yet, since I do not have information on their location
# and therefore the local_density they're in

# We want to add a "recruited" column to each row (i.e. for each individual at
# each sampling month), indicating how many offspring that individual produced 
# in that month. The aim is to assign to each row (individual) the number of 
# individuals that have that fish as a parent (father or mother), and
# were first captured 2 months after the current time point (indivuals being
# captured only 2 months after being born)

# Count the numbers of recruits per mother per month
offspringFromMothers <- pedigree %>%
    group_by(Maternity, cohort_samp) %>%
    summarize(recruited = n()) %>%
    mutate(sampling = cohort_samp - 2) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    mutate(FishID = Maternity) %>% select( -Maternity)
# Idem for the fathers
#### NO NEED NOW, there are no males
# offspringFromFathers <- pedigree %>%
#     group_by(Paternity, cohort_samp) %>%
#     summarize(recruited = n()) %>%
#     mutate(sampling = cohort_samp - 2) %>%
#     ungroup() %>%
#     mutate(FishID = Paternity) %>% select( - Paternity)
# Concatenate the recruitment information for mothers and fathers
offspringFromFishID = bind_rows(offspringFromMothers
                                #offspringFromFathers
                                ) %>%
    filter(FishID != "") %>%
    select( -cohort_samp)
# Merge this into the full data
data <- data %>% left_join(offspringFromFishID,
                           by = c("FishID", "sampling")) %>%
    mutate(recruited = ifelse(is.na(recruited), 0, recruited))

# TOCHECK!
# (Is it ok to set to 0 the number of recruits when it was NA? Also, we lose
# the ability to cross-check with the number of unsexed individuals.)
```

### Local and landscape densities

```{r }
#### TOTAL POP SIZE at each timestep ####
popSize <- data %>% group_by(sampling) %>%
    summarize(pop_size = n()) %>%
    select(sampling, pop_size)
data <- data %>% left_join(popSize, by = "sampling")

plot(popSize, type='l')

# LANDSCAPE population density at each timestep (individuals/m)
data <- data %>% mutate(land_density = pop_size/100) #total length of LL

#### LOCAL population size at each time point, per location ####
# generating a reach ID based on the upstream and downstream boundaries. This is less sensitive to typos than location, but allows a discrimination of reaches with the same midpoint (distance) but parallel, to be accounted separately.

data <- data %>% mutate(reachId = paste(upstream, downstream, sep = "-"))
data$reachId <- ifelse(grepl("NA", data$reachId), NA, data$reachId)
table(!is.na(data$reachId))

localPopSize <- data %>%
    group_by(sampling, reachId) %>%
    summarize(spot.pop = n()) %>%
    ungroup() %>%
    select(sampling, reachId, spot.pop)
data <- data %>% left_join(localPopSize, by = c("sampling", "reachId")) # pop size here&now

hist(data$spot.pop, col = "lightgrey")

# REACH LENGHT useful to calculate densities, but also to establish real
# movement
table(data$downstream-data$upstream<0.5)
# there are a few negative length, and only 3 zeros. I will assign NA to those

data$reach_l <- ifelse(data$downstream-data$upstream>0,
                       data$downstream-data$upstream,
                       NA)

# some absurd reach_lenghts, due to typos in the location name. I am removing
# these few data point, which might create troubles when calculating density
data[which(data$reach_l>50),]
stopifnot(NROW_CHECK == nrow(data))
data <- data[-which(data$reach_l>50),]
NROW_CHECK <- nrow(data)

# LOCAL POPULATION DENSITY, at each time point (and each location)
data$loc_density<-data$spot.pop/data$reach_l
hist(data$loc_density, col = "lightgrey")


# VARIANCE IN LOCAL POP DENSITY
var_density <- tapply(data$loc_density,data$sampling,var, na.rm=T)
data$var_density <- var_density[data$sampling]
```

### Movement

```{r }
# next time position
nextPosition <- data %>%
    transmute(FishID = FishID, distance.next = distance, sampling = sampling - 1) %>%
    filter(sampling > 0)
# Merge into the full data
data <- data %>% left_join(nextPosition, by = c("sampling", "FishID"))

table(!is.na(data$distance.next))
data$movement <- data$distance.next-data$distance



# Sanity check about the number of rows
stopifnot(NROW_CHECK == nrow(data))
```

### Natal dispersal

```{r }
# In order to estimate natal dispersal I'll take the offspring perspective. I
# need to find the first capture per each individual. And then check the
# mother's position two months before first capture (likely the month of birth
# for this fish). I may also remove all fish above a threshold length, to
# exclude "old" first captured individuals (which might have be born many
# months before).

# The first capture corresponds to the lowest sampling value in the mark
# recapture file.

# We build a matrix of information about mothers, checking where they were two
# months before the first capture of their offspring in the mark-recapture file.
motherIDs <- unique(data$Maternity)
# To be able to compare adult and natal dispersal, we need a few extra
# columns. Adult dispersal is calculated in a projective manner, finding the
# position at the next time step, but from the 'now' point of view (habitat,
# local and global density NOW). I then need to find those variables from the
# inset of natal dispersal (i.e. from the data belonging to the mother two
# months before first capture)

# The motherData table is built so that it can be merged with the "data" table
# by c("Maternity", "sampling")
motherData <- data %>% filter(FishID %in% motherIDs) %>%
    transmute(Maternity = FishID, 
              sampling.birth = sampling,
              distance.birth = distance,
              habitat.birth = Habitat,
              loc_density.birth = loc_density, 
              land_density.birth = land_density,
              sampling = sampling + 2, # We add two months, assuming that's the
                                       # delay between birth and first capture
              location.birth = location, 
              reach_l.birth = reach_l)
# We only want to add the mother's position once, in the row corresponding to
# the first capture.
# For that we introduce a new boolean variable, "isFirstCapture"
motherData$isFirstCapture = TRUE
data <- data %>% mutate(isFirstCapture = (sampling == firstCapture))

# Just to make sure the individuals captured are indeed new recruits, I will check their size. Individuals larger than 18 mm and heavier than .150 g are likely not new recruits. I will add this conditions to the isFirstCapture definition
table(data$sex_stage[data$isFirstCapture])
table(data$weight[data$isFirstCapture] > .150)
table(data$SL[data$isFirstCapture] > 18)

data <- data %>% 
  mutate(isFirstCapture = (sampling == firstCapture &
                             (weight <= .150 | is.na(weight)) &
                             (SL <= 18 | is.na(SL))
                           ))

data[is.na(data$isFirstCapture), c('sampling', 'firstCapture', 'weight', 'SL')]

# Now we are ready to merge, using c("Maternity", "sampling", "isFirstCapture")
data <- data %>% left_join(motherData, by = c("sampling", "Maternity", "isFirstCapture"))

# for someone to have a position at birth they have to have defined maternity
# and for the mother to be caught two months before the first capture of the
# offspring
table(!is.na(data$distance.birth))
# even less have a position at birth
data$natal_movement <- data$distance - data$distance.birth

# Checking some unrealistic distance specification before saving dataset
table(data$distance>100)
suspicious <- which(data$distance > 100 | data$distance.birth > 100)
data[suspicious, c("sex", "distance", "distance.birth")]
stopifnot(NROW_CHECK == nrow(data)) # Check before removing suspicious rows

# Note that with the following filtering step, we also remove rows for which
# the distance is NA
table(is.na(data$distance))
data <- data %>% filter(distance <= 100)
# Update NROW_CHECK
NROW_CHECK = nrow(data)
```

## Further data manipulation

Handling data to create variables to be modelled.

### Section and reach (spatial information)

```{r }
##### SECTION ##############################################
# I will create a variable called SECTION, used later to account for
# heterogeneity in the stream (to be included as a random effect in the model)

how.fine <- 5 # how long the sections will be is determined by this parameter, to be adjusted
  # the following command creates sections of the stream cut each "how.fine" meters
data$section<-cut(data$distance, seq(0,max(data$distance, na.rm=T), by=how.fine), right=FALSE)
data$section.birth<-cut(data$distance.birth, seq(0,max(data$distance, na.rm=T), by=how.fine), right=FALSE)
  
  
#### REACH ################################################
# As an alternative to section, I have manually assigned reach level random
# effect, grouping up reaches that changed slightly through time and chunks of
# the stream which appear to be self-consistent
reach_key <- read.table(file.path(here::here(),'data-raw','reach_key.txt'), header = T)
data$reach <- as.factor(reach_key$newID[match(data$location, reach_key$oldID)])
data$reach.birth <- as.factor(reach_key$newID[match(data$location.birth, reach_key$oldID)])
  
##### TIME ##############################################
data$time<-as.numeric(data$sampling)-1 # so that introduction becomes t0
data$time.birth<-as.numeric(data$sampling.birth)-1
data$sampling<-as.factor(data$sampling)
data$sampling.birth<-as.factor(data$sampling.birth)
```

### Scaling

To improve model convergence, I will take some steps following
https://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/33653_57fc7b8e5d484c909b615d8633c01d51.html:

- 1) SCALING/CENTERING local and global density in the model
- 2) INCREASE ITERATIONS (later)

I will scale the variables but keep the original in the data frame.

**WARNING**
For some reason, when left joining `s_loc_density` and `s_land_density`, this are introduced in tibble as vectors.

```{r }
##### SCALING ##############################################
# what needs to be scaled is not the local density vector in the data.frame,
# since values of local density are repeated once per each individual present
# in each pool and experiencing the same density. I need to scale it based on a
# vector of unique values of local densities found at each sampling and
# location
loc <- data %>% select(sampling, location, loc_density) %>%
    unique()

# I will only scale, but not center, local density. 
# This makes it easier to convert model preditions between scaled and unscaled values
loc$s_loc_density <- scale(loc$loc_density, center = FALSE)
loc <- loc %>% select( -loc_density)

data <- data %>% left_join(loc, by = c("sampling", "location"))
# Sanity check
stopifnot(NROW_CHECK == nrow(data))

#   Previously transferring attributes (scaling and centering value) from loc$s_loc_density
# to data$s_loc_density, so they can be retrieved later.
#   attr(x, 'string') <- value assignes a value as an attribute to the object (e.g. vector) x,
# to be called 'string':
# see: https://stat.ethz.ch/R-manual/R-devel/library/base/html/attr.html
#   The function sticky, from the package sticky, allows vector to retain the
# attributes even after subsetting, appending etc
# see: https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/sticky/vignettes/introduction.html
#   Now this approach has been replaced, since attributes conflict with some tidyverse 
# functions (e.g. sticky)

# I am now creating a list that stores all attributes and can be retrieved later:
scalingAttr <- list(loc_density = list(scale = attr(loc$s_loc_density, "scaled:scale")))


land <- data %>% select(sampling, land_density, time) %>%
    unique()
land$s_land_density <- scale(land$land_density, center = FALSE)

# time will be scaled but not centered, to keep the intercept at 0 in the models
land$s_time <- scale(land$time, center = F)
land <- land %>% select( -c(land_density, time))
data <- data %>% left_join(land, by = "sampling")
# Sanity check
stopifnot(NROW_CHECK == nrow(data))

# storing attributes
scalingAttr$land_density <- list(scale = attr(land$s_land_density, "scaled:scale"))
scalingAttr$time <- list(scale = attr(land$s_time, "scaled:scale"))
    
# scaling also time.birth
data$s_time.birth <- data$time.birth/attr(land$s_time, "scaled:scale")
```

### Habitat

```{r }
# removing weird habitat types (probably typos)
data$habitat<-ifelse(data$Habitat%in%c('S','B','N','P','R'), as.character(data$Habitat), NA)
data$habitat<-ifelse(data$habitat=='R', 'R', 'P') # simplifying and calling all non-riffle habitats pools
data$habitat.birth<-ifelse(data$habitat.birth%in%c('S','B','N','P','R'), as.character(data$habitat.birth), NA)
data$habitat.birth<-ifelse(data$habitat.birth=='R', 'R', 'P')
```

### Movement

```{r }
# I will here model dispersal as a  probability of moving or not (binomial), combined with the direction moved and the absolute distance moved
# hist(data$movement, breaks=100) # some cleansing
# an individual cannot have moved more than the total length of the stream (100m), up or downstream
data$movement<-ifelse(abs(data$movement)>100,NA,data$movement)
# given month to month discrepancies in drawing the tape-meter in the field, most fish appeared to have moved very short distances (they actually did not move, but the centerpoint of the reach they live in wobbled), inflating the probability of moving.
# I am here setting a cutoff to consider small distances (lower than the cutoff) as artifacts of this
# cutoff <- 0.5 #meters
# the probability of moving or not this is 0 if an individual has a recorded position and position.next, and has not moved more than the cutoff (apparent movement), and 1 if it has moved
data$p_moving<-ifelse(abs(data$movement)>data$reach_l/2,1,0)
# then, absolute distance moved
data$dist_moved<-ifelse(data$p_moving==1,   # if it moved
                          abs(data$movement), # absolute distance
                          NA)                 # NA otherwise
#hist(data$dist_moved, breaks=200)
# finally, direction moved
data$dir_moved<-ifelse(data$p_moving==1, # nested ifelse, to account for distance>cutoff and
                       ifelse(data$movement>0,1,0), # movement positive
                       NA)
```

### Natal movement

```{r }
# hist(data$natal_movement, breaks=200)
# same purging as for movement
data$natal_movement<-ifelse(abs(data$natal_movement)>100,NA,data$natal_movement)
# defining the probability of moving form birth
data$p_natal<-ifelse(abs(data$natal_movement)>data$reach_l.birth/2,1,0)
# then, absolute distance moved from birthplace
data$dist_natal<-ifelse(data$p_natal==1,
                        abs(data$natal_movement),
                        NA)
# hist(data$dist_natal, breaks=100)
data$dir_natal<-ifelse(data$p_natal==1, # nested ifelse, to account for distance>cutoff and
                        ifelse(data$natal_movement>0,1,0), # movement positive
                        NA)
```

### Density for natal dispersal

```{r }
data$loc_density.mid <- rep(NA, nrow(data))
data$land_density.mid <- rep(NA, nrow(data))
data$mummoved <- rep(NA, nrow(data))

# scaling  
data$s_loc_density.mid <- rep(NA, nrow(data))
data$s_land_density.mid <- rep(NA, nrow(data))

# Convert columns to character or numeric type
for (col in c("Maternity", "FishID")) {
    data[[col]] = as.character(data[[col]])
}
data[["sampling"]] = as.numeric(data[["sampling"]])

for(i in 1:nrow(data)){

    if(data$isFirstCapture[i]){

        mum = data$Maternity[i]
        when = data$sampling[i]-1

        mumWhenIndex = which(data$FishID == mum & data$sampling == when)

        # Loop for loc mid density
        if(length(mumWhenIndex) == 1){
            data$loc_density.mid[i] <- data$loc_density[mumWhenIndex]
            data$land_density.mid[i] <- data$land_density[mumWhenIndex]
            # scaled variables
            data$s_loc_density.mid[i] <- data$s_loc_density[mumWhenIndex]
            data$s_land_density.mid[i] <- data$s_land_density[mumWhenIndex]
        }

        # Loop for mother's movement
        mumWhenMinusOneIndex = which(data$FishID == mum & data$sampling == when-1)
        if(length(mumWhenMinusOneIndex) == 1){
            data$mummoved[i] <- data$p_moving[mumWhenMinusOneIndex]
        }

    } # end if loop for natal rows only

} # end for loop
```

## Clean-up and saving

```{r }
# Last sanity check
stopifnot(NROW_CHECK == nrow(data))

# Saving dataset in an R dataset format
ipmdata = data
save(ipmdata, file=file.path(here::here(), 'data', 'ipmdata.rda'))
save(scalingAttr, file = file.path(here::here(), 'data', 'scalingAttr.rda'))
```
